Document: Part 6 – Service of Documents
Part 3 of 3
==================================================
[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.42] (A list of British overseas territories is reproduced in paragraph 5.2 of Practice Direction 6B.)

## 6.43

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (1) This rule applies where a party wishes to serve a claim form or any other document under rule 6.42(1) or 6.42(2). [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (2) Where this rule applies, that party must file –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (a) a request for service of the claim form or other document specifying one or more of the methods in rule 6.42(1) or 6.42(2);

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (b) a copy of the claim form or other document;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (c) any other documents or copies of documents required by Practice Direction 6B; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (d) any translation required under rule 6.45. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (3) Where a party files the documents specified in paragraph (2), the court officer will –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (a) seal(GL) the copy of the claim form or other document; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (b) forward the documents to the Senior Master. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (4) The Senior Master will send documents forwarded under this rule –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (a) where the claim form or other document is being served through the authority designated under the Hague Convention or any other Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty, to that authority; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (b) in any other case, to the Foreign and Commonwealth Office with a request that it arranges for the claim form or other document to be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (5) An official certificate which –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (a) states that the method requested under paragraph (2)(a) has been performed and the date of such performance;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (b) states, where more than one method is requested under paragraph (2)(a), which method was used; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (c) is made by –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (i) a British Consular authority in the country where the method requested under paragraph (2)(a) was performed;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (ii) the government or judicial authorities in that country; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (iii) the authority designated in respect of that country under the a Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty, is evidence of the facts stated in the certificate. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.43] (6) A document purporting to be an official certificate under paragraph (5) is to be treated as such a certificate, unless it is proved not to be. ## Service of claim form or other document on a State

## 6.44

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (1) This rule applies where a party wishes to serve the claim form or other document on a State. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (2) In this rule, ‘State’ has the meaning given by section 14 of the State Immunity Act 1978 16 . [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (3) The party must file in the Central Office of the Royal Courts of Justice –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (a) a request for service to be arranged by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (b) a copy of the claim form or other document; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (c) any translation required under rule 6.45. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (4) The Senior Master will send the documents filed under this rule to the Foreign and Commonwealth Office with a request that it arranges for them to be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (5) An official certificate by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office stating that a claim form or other document has been duly served on a specified date in accordance with a request made under this rule is evidence of that fact. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (6) A document purporting to be such a certificate is to be treated as such a certificate, unless it is proved not to be. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (7) Where –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (a) section 12(6) of the State Immunity Act 1978 applies; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (b) the State has agreed to a method of service other than through the Foreign and Commonwealth Office, the claim form or other document may be served either by the method agreed or in accordance with this rule. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.44] (Section 12(6) of the State Immunity Act 1978 provides that section 12(1) enables the service of a claim form or other document in a manner to which the State has agreed.)

## Translation of claim form or other document

## 6.45

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (1) Except where paragraph (4) or (5) applies, every copy of the claim form or other document filed under rule 6.43 (service through foreign governments, judicial authorities etc.) or 6.44 (service of claim form or other document on a State) must be accompanied by a translation of the claim form or other document. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (2) The translation must be –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (a) in the official language of the country in which it is to be served; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (b) if there is more than one official language of that country, in any official language which is appropriate to the place in the country where the claim form or other document is to be served. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (3) Every translation filed under this rule must be accompanied by a statement by the person making it that it is a correct translation, and the statement must include that person’s name, address and qualifications for making the translation. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (4) A party is not required to file a translation of a claim form or other document filed under rule 6.43 (service through foreign governments, judicial authorities etc.) where the claim form or other document is to be served –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (a) in a country of which English is an official language; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (b) on a British citizen (within the meaning of the British Nationality Act 1981 17 ), unless a Civil Procedure Convention or Treaty requires a translation. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.45] (5) A party is not required to file a translation of a claim form or other document filed under rule 6.44 (service of claim form or other document on a State) where English is an official language of the State in which the claim form or other document is to be served. ## Undertaking to be responsible for expenses

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Undertaking to be responsible for expenses] 6.46 Every request for service filed under rule 6.43 (service through foreign governments, judicial authorities etc.) or rule 6.44 (service of claim form or other document on a State) must contain an undertaking by the person making the request –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Undertaking to be responsible for expenses] (a) to be responsible for all expenses incurred by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office or foreign judicial authority; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > Undertaking to be responsible for expenses] (b) to pay those expenses to the Foreign and Commonwealth Office or foreign judicial authority on being informed of the amount. ## Proof of service before obtaining judgment

## 6.47 Where

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.47 Where] (a) a hearing is fixed when the claim form is issued;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.47 Where] (b) the claim form is served on a defendant out of the jurisdiction; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.47 Where] (c) that defendant does not appear at the hearing,

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.47 Where] the claimant may not obtain judgment against the defendant until the claimant files written evidence that the claim form has been duly served in accordance with this Part. ## V SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS FROM FOREIGN COURTS OR TRIBUNALS

## Scope of this Section

## 6.48 This Section –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.48 This Section –] (a) applies to the service in England and Wales of any document in connection with civil or commercial proceedings in a foreign court or tribunal

## Interpretation

## 6.49 In this Section –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.49 In this Section –] (a) ‘convention country’ means a country in relation to which there is a Civil Procedure Convention (which has the same meaning as in rule 6.31(c));

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.49 In this Section –] (b) ‘foreign court or tribunal’ means a court or tribunal in a country outside of the United Kingdom; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.49 In this Section –] (c) ‘process server’ means –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.49 In this Section –] (i) a process server appointed by the Lord Chancellor to serve documents to which this Section applies, or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.49 In this Section –] (ii) the process server’s agent. ## Request for service

## 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –] (a) a written request for service –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –] (i) where the foreign court or tribunal is in a convention country, from a consular or other authority of that country; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –] (ii) from the Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs, with a recommendation that service should be effected;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –] (b) a translation of that request into English;

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –] (c) two copies of the document to be served; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.50 The Senior Master will serve a document to which this Section applies upon receipt of –] (d) unless the foreign court or tribunal certifies that the person to be served understands the language of the document, two copies of a translation of it into English. ## Method of service

## 6.51 The Senior Master will determine the method of service. ## After service

## 6.52

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (1) Where service of a document has been effected by a process server, the process server must –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (a) send to the Senior Master a copy of the document, and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (i) proof of service; or

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (ii) a statement why the document could not be served; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (b) if the Senior Master directs, specify the costs incurred in serving or attempting to serve the document. [PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (2) The Senior Master will send to the person who requested service –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (a) a certificate, sealed with the seal of the Senior Courts for use out of the jurisdiction, stating –

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (i) when and how the document was served or the reason why it has not been served; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (ii) where appropriate, an amount certified by a costs judge to be the costs of serving or attempting to serve the document; and

[PART 6 – SERVICE OF DOCUMENTS > 6.52] (b) a copy of the document. ## Footnotes
